title: AI Forms Generation Framework tool spec (tool.json)

$schema.description: This schema, for editor completion and checking.

executable.description: The program to run (on PATH or a full path). With an Interpreter, an optional override of it.

interpreter.description: Run Script with "pwsh" (PowerShell; Windows PowerShell if pwsh is missing) or "python" — UTF-8 output, no buffering, no profile/policy surprises. The field arguments (after fixedArgs) become the script's arguments.

script.description: The script for Interpreter; a relative path is relative to the spec file.

timeoutSeconds.description: Stop a run (the whole process tree) after this many seconds; omit for no limit.

runButton.description: Caption of the Run button; "&" marks the Alt access key.

busyOverlay.description: Dim the window while running (hides the live log).

dark.description: The dark variant of the theme.

tint.description: How strongly backgrounds take the accent's hue, 0–1.

themeButton.description: Show a "Theme…" button so the user can pick colours (saved with the settings).

sunkenFields.description: Draw every input field as a sunken Direct3D card with a focus-glow ring (the WinForms Direct3D look), the same effect the Results grid already gets. Best with a dark Theme and "buttonStyle": "glow".

env.description: Environment variables set for the tool's process, e.g. { "MYTOOL_PROGRESS_STDOUT": "1" } to make a script emit its ##PROGRESS## / ChoicesFromMarker markers.

buttonStyle.description: How buttons are drawn: "flat", "raised" or "glow" (AiFgfEffects); absent = the application's default. A choice the user makes in the "Theme…" dialog wins; flat where an effect cannot be drawn.

renderer.description: How ButtonStyle ("raised"/"glow") is actually drawn: absent (default) for the cross-platform look (WinForms: Direct3D 12; Avalonia: a drop shadow), or "direct3d" to ask Avalonia for the real Direct3D 12 rendering too (the WinForms look: buttons and field focus glow) — only on Windows, and only when the app referenced the experimental add-on (AI_FGF.Avalonia.Direct3D) and it could initialise; otherwise this is ignored and the drop shadow is used, unchanged. WinForms already draws with Direct3D 12 and ignores this field.

resultsCsv.description: After a successful run, load this CSV into the Results tab; may use {Key} placeholders.

warningCodes.description: Exit codes that mean "finished with a warning", with a message: { "3010": "Reboot required" }.

failureMessages.description: Readable messages for failing exit codes: { "16": "Fatal error" }.

settingsKey.description: Key under which settings are saved (default: derived from the title; "" = do not persist).

label.description: The button's caption (an ampersand marks the Alt mnemonic).

executable.description: Another program to run; empty runs the spec's executable.

fixedArgs.description: Arguments in place of the spec's fixedArgs (e.g. ["stop"]); omitted keeps the spec's.

fields.description: The keys of the fields it passes; omitted passes every field (as the Run button does).

items.description: One more button of a ToolSpec (.NET 11): its own command from the same fields - "Stop" beside "Start", "Check" before "Deploy".

actions.description: More buttons beside Run (.NET 11), each running its own command from the same fields: "Start" / "Stop" of a service, "Check" before "Deploy". An action replaces fixedArgs, and may run another executable and pass only some fields. The Run button stays the spec's own command.

key.description: Stable key (settings, presets, {Key} placeholders). Required, unique.

label.description: Caption shown next to the input. Required.

lines.description: Visible lines of a memo field (default 4). Memo lines never wrap.

maxLines.description: A memo grows with its text up to this many lines before it scrolls (default 12).

readOnly.description: A memo that shows text instead of taking input.

switch.description: A flag shown as an on/off switch instead of a check box (.NET 11, WinForms and Avalonia; a check box on .NET 10).

password.description: A text field whose input is hidden (a password, a token); never saved with the form's settings (.NET 11; plain text on .NET 10).

radio.description: A choice shown as radio buttons, all choices at once, instead of a drop-down (.NET 11; a drop-down on .NET 10). Not with editable.

kind.description: The input: text, file, folder, choice, number, flag or memo.

required.description: The value must not be empty (shown as "Label *").

default.description: Initial value: text, a choice, a number (4 or "4") or a flag (true/false).

placeholder.description: Grey hint text shown while the field is empty.

choices.description: Choice: the allowed values (shown in a drop-down list).

editable.description: Choice: allow typing values that are not in the list.

choicesFromMarker.description: Fill a type-ahead combo live from the tool's own output: each stdout line <marker>|value (e.g. "##FEATURE##") adds value to this field's drop-down, and the marker lines are hidden from the log. Turns a text field into an editable combo (a choice keeps its listed items and gains the discovered ones). The tool must print the markers — usually gated by an Env variable. Run once (e.g. with the field empty) to populate it.

decimals.description: Number: digits after the decimal point (shown and passed).

pattern.description: Text/File/Folder/Choice: value must match this regex.

patternMessage.description: The message shown when the value does not match Pattern.

arg.description: How the value becomes command-line arguments: "-o" emits -o value (skipped when empty); "--level={value}" emits one token ({value} or the field's own {Key}; another field's {Key} is that field's value); for a flag, the argument is emitted when checked. Leave empty and set Positional for a bare value.

positional.description: Emit the value as a bare argument, after all options, in field order.

enabledWhen.description: Enable this field only while a condition holds: "Key" (set / checked), "!Key", "Key=value", "Key!=value". A disabled field is not validated and not passed to the tool.

visibleWhen.description: Show this field only while a condition holds (same syntax); hidden fields take no space.

items.description: One input of a ToolSpec: how it looks, how it validates, how it becomes arguments.

fields.description: The inputs, in the order shown; each becomes arguments as its arg / positional say.

resolvedScript.description: The script path, resolved against BaseDirectory when relative.

description: A declarative description of a tool form — the "template" that turns a short description of a command-line tool into a correct SpecToolForm (WinForms or Avalonia) without writing UI code: var spec = ToolSpec.FromFile("tool.json"); if (spec.Validate().Any(i => i.IsError)) … AiFgfApp.Run(() => new SpecToolForm(spec)); JSON is case-insensitive and tolerates comments and trailing commas, so it can be edited by hand.
